_comment: Maintainer-decision dispositions for issue #671 (launch-watch needs-human, 2026-11-09), plus the two carried needs-human rows from the issue #571 review (reports/launch-watch/2026-11-04-issue-571-review.json) that the 2026-11-05 candidate-queue follow-up left open. The original scan records remain unchanged. Approved rows name the product identity for bring-up; the bring-up itself lands in its own PR through the standard scoped engine run. No score or rank is set here.

dispositions.name: Aider → speech-to-text
dispositions.reason: The linked page is a recorded coding-assistant session, not a speech-to-text API. Same evidence and outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://aider.chat/docs/recordings/dont-drop-original-read-files.html — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.

dispositions.name: Airwallex → fp-a
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-09: the page documents expense policy enforcement, receipt matching, accounts payable, and close speed. It names no financial models, forecasting, scenario planning, budget-vs-actuals, or board reporting, so the fp-a definition is not met. Airwallex's expense-management placement is separately in flight on the 2026-11-09 launch-watch scan PR (#670).
evidence: https://www.airwallex.com/global/spend-management/spend-ai — fetched 2026-11-09; capabilities listed are policy enforcement ("Enforce your policy in real time"), receipt capture/matching, duplicate detection, and AP linking; no forecasting or budget-vs-actuals surface.
open-rankings/categories.json fp-a definition: financial models, forecasts, scenario planning, budget-vs-actuals, and board reporting on connected books.

dispositions.name: Google Antigravity → docs-platforms
dispositions.reason: The linked page is the product's own installation guide. Having documentation does not make an agentic IDE a documentation authoring and publishing platform. Same outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started/ — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.

dispositions.name: Claude → self-hosted-assistants
dispositions.reason: The launch describes a hosted model and API, not an open-source assistant runtime runnable on user-owned infrastructure, so the self-hosted-assistants definition is not met. Anthropic affiliation is noted per the house rules; this row changes no ranked number for any Anthropic product. Same outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5 — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.
open-rankings/categories.json self-hosted-assistants definition: open-source personal AI assistant runtimes you run on your own machine, keys, and messengers.

dispositions.name: GitHub Copilot → durable-workflows
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-09 against both the GA changelog and the gh-aw documentation: GitHub Agentic Workflows compiles Markdown workflows into standard Actions YAML and documents sandboxing, read-only defaults, safe outputs, and threat detection. Neither source documents checkpointed execution or exact resume after failure, so the durable-workflows definition is not met.
evidence: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-github-agentic-workflows-generally-available — fetched 2026-11-09; "compiles them into standard Actions YAML"; safeguards cover sandboxing and threat detection, not checkpoint/resume.
https://github.github.com/gh-aw/ — fetched 2026-11-09; no checkpointing, resume, or state-persistence feature documented; `max-turns`/`max-ai-credits` are runaway caps, not recovery.
open-rankings/categories.json durable-workflows definition: durable execution engines that checkpoint long-running code and resume exactly where failures left off.

dispositions.name: Groq → frontier-models
dispositions.reason: The source credits Meta as the model developer and describes Groq hosting inference. Inference hosting does not make Groq a frontier model developer. The page also dates to April 2024. Same outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://groq.com/blog/12-hours-later-groq-is-running-llama-3-instruct-8-70b-by-meta-ai-on-its-lpu-inference-enginge — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.

dispositions.name: Groq → llm-evals-observability
dispositions.reason: The source is inference hosting, not tracing, evaluation, or observability software. Same outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://groq.com/blog/12-hours-later-groq-is-running-llama-3-instruct-8-70b-by-meta-ai-on-its-lpu-inference-enginge — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.

dispositions.name: Mastra → ai-code-review
dispositions.reason: Span Queries filters and aggregates execution traces for a coding agent to consume. That is trace tooling, not an autonomous pull-request review product. Same outcome as the 2026-11-04 review of the identical row.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-span-queries — reviewed 2026-11-04 (issue #571 review); row regenerated unchanged in the 2026-11-09 scan.

dispositions.name: Mastra → ai-memory
dispositions.reason: Approved as the distinct product identity mastra-knowledge, not the generic Mastra framework identity. The 2026-11-04 review deferred on design-partner-only access; the public alpha (added in @mastra/core@1.82.0) resolves that: installation is public, and the docs name the agent tools knowledge_search, knowledge_read, and knowledge_page. Documented alpha limitations (no scope-isolation guarantee, no built-in importers, no retention) are retained as evidence for the bring-up. Bring-up runs the standard scoped engine run in its own PR.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/overview — fetched 2026-11-09; alpha in @mastra/core@1.82.0; tools knowledge_search/knowledge_read/knowledge_page; "the alpha doesn't guarantee isolation between scopes yet"; "no built-in importers or retention yet".
https://mastra.ai/blog/announcing-mastra-knowledge — public alpha release post.
reports/2026-11-05-candidate-queue-followup.md — prepared mastra-knowledge in ai-memory.

dispositions.name: Mastra → ai-support-agents
dispositions.reason: A knowledge base that agents can search, read, and update is not an autonomous support agent that resolves customer conversations end-to-end. The ai-memory placement (this review, mastra-knowledge) owns this launch.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-knowledge — fetched 2026-11-09 window; describes agent-facing knowledge tools, not customer-conversation resolution.

dispositions.name: Mastra → card-issuing
dispositions.reason: The launch is a partner/agency program for consultancies building Mastra agents. The keyword match (program, network, agent) is lexical noise against the card-issuing definition.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/mastra-agency-program — headline describes a certified-agency network, not card creation or authorization APIs.

dispositions.name: Mastra → document-extraction
dispositions.reason: Knowledge is a store agents search, read, and write. The launch documents no PDF/scan/spreadsheet-to-structured-output extraction API; the keyword match (scan, agent, search) is lexical noise.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-knowledge — describes knowledge-base tools for agents, not document AI extraction.

dispositions.name: Mastra → game-engines
dispositions.reason: The Custom Harness Program is a services program for building agent systems on Mastra. The keyword match (engine, build, agent) is lexical noise against the game-engines definition.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/announcing-custom-harness-program — forward-deployed engineering program, not a game engine or real-time 3D framework.

dispositions.name: Mastra → llm-evals-observability
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-09: the latency metrics attach to Mastra spans for agents and models running on the Mastra platform, Studio, or self-hosted Mastra projects. That is framework-scoped telemetry, not an observability platform for LLM apps generally. The post mentions trace imports for outside data without documenting that surface; revisit if Mastra documents non-Mastra tracing as a product surface.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-latency-metrics — fetched 2026-11-09; "track latency metrics for every agent and model call in Mastra platform and Studio"; works on Mastra platform and self-hosted Mastra projects via storage.observability backends.

dispositions.name: Mastra Code → ai-coding (carried from the issue #571 review)
dispositions.reason: Approved as the distinct product identity mastra-code, not the generic Mastra framework identity. Verified live 2026-11-09: a terminal coding agent installable today (npm install -g mastracode, Node >= 22.19.0) with documented headless automation (mastracode --prompt with json/jsonl output and exit codes; runMC Node API for CI). On-axis for ai-coding; the headless CLI and Node API are the agentic surface. Bring-up runs the standard scoped engine run in its own PR.
evidence: https://code.mastra.ai/ — fetched 2026-11-09; install commands and TUI/CLI/Node surfaces documented.
https://code.mastra.ai/headless — fetched 2026-11-09; non-interactive CLI flags, output modes, exit codes, runMC API, resolution policies.
